topology: Classic IOS EIGRP AS100 diamond R1–R2/R3–R4 with PC1 behind R1 and SRV1 behind R4. R4 Loopback0 198.51.100.1/32 is an independent offset-list control prefix. Practice begins with R1 Gi0/1 bandwidth100000 instead of1000000 Kbit/s. Final primary metric10240/RD7680 uses R2; the R3 feasible alternate is20480/RD7680.
implemented: Sixteenth ENARSI Layer3 Technologies catalog entry with independent practice/completed documents, six-row addressing/metric plan, staged instructions, executable reference/verification commands and current-origin/path/query permalinks. Existing simulation engine, networking logic, UI layout, artwork, terminal and styling are unchanged.

Classic metric calculations are verified against actual RIB/CEF and delivered UPDATE vectors: 256×(10000000/minimum bandwidth + sum of outgoing interface delays in tens of microseconds). Local incorrect bandwidth produces primary33280 versus alternate20480. Repair returns primary10240 and keeps four actual neighbor pairs.

Initial diagnosis requires three accepted server requests and matched replies over R1/R3/R4, plus three reverse requests over R4/R2/R1. Corrected bidirectional service traffic uses R2. HTTP requires a complete actual200 service body, not a status label alone.

Local R1 Gi0/1 delay100 changes the R2 candidate total to33280 while RD remains7680 and historical FD remains10240. Delivered requests prefer R3 while reverse requests continue through R2; restoring delay10 needs fresh primary-path replies.

Remote R2 Gi0/1 bandwidth156250 gives an exact inverse-bandwidth term64, local R2 service metric21504 and R1 candidate24064/RD21504. R1 prefers R3 while reverse traffic stays on R2. Restoring1000000 requires fresh delivered traffic. Bandwidth metadata does not change interface speed or link state.

Prepared standard ACL10 selects only192.168.40.0/24 and is not bound as a data-plane filter. R1 inbound offset16384 on Gi0/1 changes its R2 total to26624 with RD7680. R2 outbound offset16384 on Gi0/0 changes advertised RD to24064 and remote total to26624 while its own RIB remains7680. Both exercises require successful service traffic over R3, reverse traffic over R2, and control-loopback traffic still over R2 at10240, followed by fresh restored probes to both prefixes.

K3 mismatch on R2 removes its two actual EIGRP adjacencies while physical links stay up. Both service directions must traverse R3 during the mismatch. Restoring default K values recovers all four pairs and requires fresh R2 traffic; matching a nondefault metric policy is not the intended repair.

Per-attempt config/route epochs reject stale packets and config-only toggles. Six live and eight observed criteria produce practice0/14, original diagnosis1/14, repaired baseline9/14 and full14/14. Completed reference provides six live checks only. YAML retains earned stages while dropping runtime; fresh practice starts without observations. Canonical rendered config replays into clean routers and saved reload repairs an unsaved metric error.
scope: Classic IOS IPv4 internal EIGRP bandwidth/delay metrics, selective inbound/outbound offset lists and K-value adjacency troubleshooting. No engine changes or new CLI commands were necessary. No fresh CML capture, physical throughput/latency equivalence, per-packet load sharing, hardware timing equivalence, named wide-metric exercise or IPv6 offset-list support is claimed.
